name: Theresia Gouw
forbes_bio: Theresia Gouw launched Acrew Capital, an early-stage venture capital firm in 2019; it now manages $1.7 billion in gross assets.
In 2014 she cofounded venture capital firm Aspect Ventures with Jennifer Fonstad; in 2019 the two women parted ways.
Gouw earned her stripes in the VC world at Accel, where she spent 15 years and was the firm's first female partner.
Successful investments she led while at Accel included bets on real estate site Trulia and cybersecurity firm Imperva.
She is chair of education nonprofit DonorsChoose and a board member at ONE, a nonprofit focused on ending poverty.
forbes_facts: Gouw has appeared on the Forbes Midas List of the most successful venture capitalists, seven times.
An engineering major at Brown University, she considered switching to sociology but was persuaded not to by her father.

name: Sun Xishuang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2015-2021); Hurun Global (2014-2024); Hurun China (2009-2024)
forbes_bio: Sun Xishuang and his main business, Dalian Yifang, are business partners of fellow Chinese billionaire Wang Jianlin's Wanda Group.
Dalian Yifang and Wanda have collaborated on resorts at Changbai Mountain in northern China and in the Xishuangbanna rainforest in the south.

name: Christopher MacMillan
forbes_bio: Christopher MacMillan is one of 21 billionaire heirs to Cargill, the world's biggest agriculture business.
His great-great-grandfather, W.W. Cargill, founded the business as a single grain warehouse on the end of an Iowa railroad line in 1865.
The family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill, which did $154 billion in 2025 sales across food, agriculture, financial and industrial divisions.
He's one of nine billionaire siblings who inherited stakes in the company from their father John H.  MacMillan III, who died in 2008.

name: Dai Jun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2025-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Dai Jun is chairman and CEO of RoboTechnik Intelligent Technology, a Suzhou-based company that makes assembly and testing equipment for optical systems.
Dai founded RoboTechnik in 2011 to manufacture equipment for solar cells. It pivoted to optics in 2020 by acquiring a stake in German optical device assemble and testing equipment maker FiconTEC.

RoboTechnik completed its full acquisition of FiconTEC in 2025, which valued the company at $279 million. It came as tech giants such as Google, Meta and Nvidia are switching to light-based transmission amid the AI boom.
Prior to founding RoboTechnik, Dai was general manager of Chinese electronic components maker Yuanjiesheng.

name: Yoshiko Shinohara
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2017-2018); Hurun Global (2018)
forbes_bio: Yoshiko Shinohara became Japan's first self-made female billionaire in early 2017.
She founded Temp Holdings, a temporary staffing company, in 1973 after a stint as a secretary.
Shinohara, who owns a minority stake in the firm, retired from her longtime position as chairman in April 2016 but remains chairman emeritus.
The company, now Persol Holdings, had $7.6 billion in revenue in the fiscal year ended in March 2022.
forbes_facts: Shinohara founded the company in her Tokyo apartment.
Her foundation endows scholarships to help students who are training to become nurses, daycare staff and social workers.

name: Chanchai Ruayrungruang
forbes_bio: Chinese-Thai businessman Chanchai Ruayrungruang, also known as Yan Bin, leads the privately held Reignwood Group.
Reignwood's best-known assets are Reignwood Centre - an office, hotel and retail complex in Beijing, and the Pine Valley golf course, also in Beijing.
Chanchai started the business in Thailand in 1984 and moved into China a dozen years later.

name: Dexter Salna
forbes_bio: Dexter Salna was an early employee at Canadian tech company Constellation Software.
Constellation Software, also known as CSI, acquires, manages and builds software businesses.
A Harvard MBA, Salna was one of the original employees at Constellation, founded by fellow billionaire Mark Leonard.
From 2004 to 2023, he was president and CEO of Perseus Group, an operating division within Constellation with a portfolio of vertical market software companies spanning auto repair to homebuilding.

name: Ronnen Harary
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2018-2022); Hurun Global (2018-2019); Wikidata (2021)
forbes_bio: Ronnen Harary is the cofounder and co-CEO of Spin Master Corp., known for its popular kids' toys like Hatchimals, Air Hogs and Paw Patrol.
Harary started the company in 1994 with his childhood friend Anton Rabie.
Armed with $10,000, Rabie and Harary released Spin Master's first toy in 1994. It was called "Earth Buddy" and resembled a Chia Pet.
Spin Master had its IPO in 2015.
Spin Master is now a $1.6 billion (sales) company, which employs over 1,500 people in 16 countries.
forbes_facts: Rabie and Harary reportedly met at summer camp in Ontario when they were both 11 years old.
Spin Master made toys for the popular children's TV show, The Wiggles.
In 2021, Spin Master acquired the Rubik's cube for $50 million.
